result.summary: I've treated this as an emergency and escalated it to the team as high priority. Mr Finch is 84, has a heart condition and lives alone. He has had no heating or hot water since 6 October, overnight temperatures are around 3C, and he now says he feels dizzy. The landlord hasn't answered three emails and is away until 20 October. Once the case was escalated, I booked Calder Heating to attend urgently without landlord approval. I sent Mr Finch safety advice, including to call NHS 111 now and 999 if he gets worse, and queued a phone call to the landlord's mobile to explain and ask approval for up to £200.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 001: Mr Finch is 84, lives alone and has a heart condition. His heating and hot water stopped on 6 October and overnight temperatures are around 3C. Events 002–005: the landlord got three emails with no reply and is away until 20 October. Event 006: the tenant now feels dizzy. This fits the emergency rule for no heating for a vulnerable tenant in cold weather. The classifiers agreed: severity emergency 1.0, safety risk 0.93, safety concern in the tenant's SMS 0.9. Approval can't block emergency safety work, so I escalated as high priority first and then booked the engineer. I recorded the reason in the escalation and in the assignment.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep waiting for the landlord and chase again (lessons #15 and #23)
alternatives_considered.why_not: Those lessons are for routine jobs. Here a vulnerable tenant with a heart condition is in a cold home and has symptoms, so waiting until 20 October risks his health.

alternatives_considered.option: Only escalate, without booking an engineer
alternatives_considered.why_not: That leaves him without heat until a person picks it up. The rules say to book urgent attendance and escalate at the same time.

alternatives_considered.option: Send another email to the landlord
alternatives_considered.why_not: Email isn't reaching them because of the out-of-office. I queued a call to the mobile number on file instead.
